title: Leading teams across organizations and cultures
blurb: Apply clear boundaries, realistic role allocation and social cohesion to teams that span organizations, cultures and locations.
question: At Pinewick Home and Garden, the store operations team is spread across stores in England and Wales and rarely meets the e-commerce team at head office. Trust between the two teams is low. Which action is MOST LIKELY to build social cohesion?

teach.h: Temporary, mixed teams need a different lead
teach.body: A project team is brought together for a limited time, often from several organizations: the business, users and suppliers, each with its own culture. A temporary leader may find authority harder to exercise, and team members may be more senior than the project manager. So leadership works through collaboration and co-creation, not the organization chart. PRINCE2 calls the underlying skill cultural intelligence: relating and working across cultures.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3, 3.3.1; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3

teach.h: Across organizations and cultures: clear boundaries
teach.body: When people come from different organizations and cultures, set clear boundaries within which people can flex. Inside the boundaries, people use their own judgement and self-manage; at the edges, they know to involve others. A delegation matrix is a practical way to do this: for each decision area it shows who decides and who is involved, for example what an external adviser decides and where they only advise.

teach.caption: Agreed in the project kickoff workshop (team delegation matrix topic) to simplify decisions and empower self-management.

teach.h: One person per role? Often not
teach.body: Ideally an organization would assign a separate person to each required role, but this is often impractical. Roles are commonly combined in one person or shared between people. What matters is that each role reflects people's capability, authority and availability, and that gaps are spotted and handled, for example by upskilling or moving a responsibility to someone better placed. Waiting for a perfect one-to-one match is not the answer.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.2; PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3.2

teach.h: Social cohesion: plan it, do not order it
teach.body: Whether teams work virtually, in person or hybrid, how people work with each other needs careful thought, both to use their time well and to build social cohesion: the trust and relationships that make a group a team. Co-location helps relationships grow naturally in unstructured moments, but mandating it is unlikely to work. Teams that are virtual, at a distance or hybrid may need extra activities: sync co-location days for key people and teams, and allow time for less structured conversation online.

teach.caption: A tight agenda can make a meeting efficient, but it does not build relationships.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Pinewick click and collect (AS3)
teach.body: Pinewick's e-commerce team (Scrum, head office), store operations team (Kanban, spread across stores) and supplier Tallis rarely meet, and Tallis staff either wait for approval or change interface details unasked. Project manager Patrick Dunne runs a kickoff workshop where the teams agree a delegation matrix: Tallis decides interface design, advises on website screens. He syncs co-location days for key people around each release and keeps the first minutes of online calls unstructured. Sophie Draper combines leading the store team with product ownership for it.

teach.h: Where each people decision is recorded
head: Decision
Where it goes
rows: Who decides or advises per decision area
Who has which skills, and gaps
teach.caption: Team structure and role descriptions are organization practice products (7.3.2); the two matrices are its techniques (7.4).

teach.text: Classic traps: unclear decision rights are fixed by a DELEGATION matrix, not a skill matrix. Weak cohesion is not fixed by mandating co-location or by tighter agendas; plan how people work together and add relationship time. And one person per role is ideal but often impractical: combining or sharing roles is normal.

items: Project teams are temporary and mixed; lead through collaboration and cultural intelligence.
Across organizations and cultures: set clear boundaries within which people can flex (4.3.1).
A delegation matrix shows who decides and who is involved per decision area.
One person per role is often impractical; combine or share roles by capability and availability (4.3.2).
Build social cohesion deliberately: synced co-location days, unstructured online time (4.3.3).
Mandated co-location and formal agendas are unlikely to build cohesion.

summary: You can now lead teams that span organizations, cultures and locations: setting clear boundaries with a delegation matrix, combining or sharing roles realistically, and building social cohesion with synced co-location days and unstructured time rather than mandates. You can also say where each of these decisions is recorded.

A.q: At Larkspur Rail, developers from Coinbridge Payments, the supplier building automatic payments, either wait for Larkspur's approval on every interface detail or change payment rules without telling the app team. The two companies have very different working cultures. Which action is MOST LIKELY to help the teams work well together?
options: Set clear boundaries within which Coinbridge staff can flex
Build a team skill matrix showing each person's expertise
Require Coinbridge staff to work in Larkspur's offices daily
Ask the project board to approve each interface decision
A.why: Working across organizations and cultures needs clear boundaries within which people can flex (4.3.1), for example a delegation matrix showing what Coinbridge decides and where it advises.

whyNot.1: A skill matrix shows capabilities and gaps; it does not clarify who may decide what.
whyNot.2: Mandating co-location is unlikely to be effective; it does not settle decision rights either.
whyNot.3: Sending every detail to the board removes self-management and slows delivery.

A.q: At Pinewick, the store operations team works from stores across England and Wales and meets the head office e-commerce team mostly in short online calls. The project manager notices that the two teams do not know or trust each other. Which action is MOST LIKELY to build social cohesion?
options: Require both teams to work from head office every day
Give every online call a strict agenda and timekeeper
Sync co-location days for key people from both teams
Agree a delegation matrix covering both of the teams
A.why: For teams that are at a distance or hybrid, building social cohesion may need extra activities such as syncing co-location days for key people and teams, focused on key relationships (4.3.3).

whyNot.0: Co-location helps relationships, but mandating it is unlikely to build cohesion.
whyNot.1: A formal agenda can make calls efficient, but cohesion grows from less structured time together.
whyNot.3: A delegation matrix clarifies decision rights; it does not build relationships between the teams.

A.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's digital team has three people, and the project manager cannot find a separate person for every role in the project's team structure without hiring. What does PRINCE2 Agile guidance suggest?
options: Delay delivery until each role has its own person
Recruit so that every role has a dedicated holder
Leave the unfilled roles empty until next stage
Combine or share roles by capability and time
A.why: One person per role is ideal but often impractical (4.3.2); roles can be combined or shared, matched to capability, authority and availability.

whyNot.0: Delaying for a perfect one-to-one match is not needed; combining roles is normal.
whyNot.1: Hiring for every role is not required and may not be affordable within a fixed budget.
whyNot.2: Leaving roles empty means their responsibilities go unmet; combine or share them instead.

B.q: Larkspur's data team uses an external university adviser on machine learning. Nobody is sure whether she decides how the model's results are explained to passengers or only gives advice. The project manager wants to make this transparent, decision area by decision area. Which technique should be used?
options: A team skill matrix
A delegation matrix
A project canvas
A cumulative flow diagram
B.why: A delegation matrix makes responsibilities and decision authority transparent: for each decision area, who decides and who is involved (7.4.3). It sets the clear boundaries 4.3.1 calls for.

whyNot.0: A skill matrix shows skills and gaps, not decision authority.
whyNot.2: The project canvas is the one-page business justification.
whyNot.3: A cumulative flow diagram shows work in each workflow state over time.

B.q: During initiation at Callowmere University, the project manager agrees which web team members will be on campus, how Northmere Systems' developers will work remotely, and which online tools both will use for transparency. In which product should these arrangements be recorded?
options: The role descriptions
The commercial management approach
The project management team structure
The communication management approach
B.why: The project management team structure covers who is involved, how they work together, and arrangements for co-location or remote teams with tools for transparency and rich communication (7.3.2).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions hold each role's specific responsibilities, not working arrangements.
whyNot.1: The commercial management approach covers procurement and the contract with Northmere.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach covers means and frequency of communication and feedback across the ecosystem, not team working arrangements.

B.q: At Callowmere, joint online meetings between the web team and Northmere's remote developers are tense, and people only speak about agenda items. The project manager proposes tighter agendas so meetings finish sooner. Which alternative BEST builds social cohesion?
options: Allow time for less structured conversation online
Require Northmere's developers to work on campus
Replace joint meetings with written status updates
Set clear rules on who may speak at each meeting
B.why: Social cohesion in remote or hybrid teams can be helped by allowing time for less structured conversation online (4.3.3).

whyNot.1: Mandating co-location is unlikely to build cohesion.
whyNot.2: Written updates reduce contact further and do not build relationships.
whyNot.3: More structure on meetings makes them efficient, not cohesive.

C.q: At Pinewick, the project manager is worried that the store operations team, spread across many stores, has weak relationships with the head office team. He orders all store team members to relocate to head office for the whole project. Is this an appropriate way to build social cohesion, and why?
options: Yes, because co-location helps relationships to grow naturally
Yes, because a Kanban team needs a single physical board
No, because ordering co-location is unlikely to build cohesion
No, because agile teams are expected to work fully remotely
C.why: Co-location can help, but mandating it is unlikely to be effective; how people work together should be planned, for example with synced co-location days for key people (4.3.3).

whyNot.0: True that co-location helps, but the verdict is wrong: ordering it is unlikely to build cohesion.
whyNot.1: Kanban boards can be digital; this does not justify the mandate.
whyNot.3: Agile teams can be co-located, remote or hybrid; there is no expectation of full remote working.

C.q: In Larkspur's project kickoff workshop, the app team, the data team and the Coinbridge team agree a matrix showing that Coinbridge decides payment gateway design and advises on app screens, while the product owner decides story priority. Is this an appropriate application of leading teams across organizations, and why?
options: Yes, because it shows each person's skills and training needs
Yes, because it sets clear boundaries within which people flex
No, because the project manager should decide cross-team matters
No, because supplier decisions must be approved by the board
C.why: Working across organizations and cultures needs clear boundaries within which people can flex (4.3.1); a delegation matrix agreed in the kickoff workshop does exactly that.

whyNot.0: That describes a team skill matrix; this matrix shows decision rights.
whyNot.2: Centralizing decisions with the project manager removes self-management within boundaries.
whyNot.3: The board sets tolerances; it does not approve routine supplier design decisions.

C.q: At Draycott, the project manager insists that every role in the team structure must have its own separate person before initiation can start. This delays the project by two months while the company recruits. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because each role needs a dedicated person to be accountable
Yes, because the principle of defined roles requires one per role
No, because roles are defined after the initiation stage is done
No, because one person per role is ideal but often impractical
C.why: Ideally each role would have its own person, but this is often impractical; roles can be combined or shared (4.3.2). Delaying two months against a fixed end date is not justified.

whyNot.0: Accountability does not need a separate person per role; combined roles keep clear accountability.
whyNot.1: Defined roles and responsibilities can be met with combined or shared roles.
whyNot.2: Roles are defined in starting up and initiation, not after initiation.

reteach.title: A touring band with session players
reteach.question: A band hires session players from other bands for a tour. What keeps the shows tight?

blocks.body: Session players need to know where they can improvise (their solo) and where they follow the band (the chorus): clear boundaries within which they can flex. Not every part has its own player, so people double up. And the band does not order everyone to share a bus for months; it plans a few days together before key shows and leaves time just to talk.

blocks.h: Three moves for a mixed team

blocks.text: Ordering people together is not cohesion. Tight agendas are not cohesion. Plan the time together around key relationships.

explain.body: Across organizations and cultures, set clear boundaries within which people can flex. A delegation matrix shows, per decision area, who decides and who is involved.

test.q: Easterholm's Abacus Care Software developers keep asking the council before every small interface choice, slowing the digital team. Which action BEST applies the guidance on leading teams across organizations?
options: Ask the board to approve interface choices
Hold weekly status calls with Abacus staff
Agree boundaries within which Abacus can flex
Have Abacus staff join the digital team on site
test.why: Clear boundaries within which people can flex let the supplier decide routine matters and involve others at the edges (4.3.1).

whyNot.0: Board approval for small choices adds delay and removes self-management.
whyNot.1: Status calls share information but do not settle who may decide.
whyNot.3: Co-location may help relationships, but it does not clarify decision rights.

explain.body: Ideally one person per role, but often impractical. Combine or share roles so they reflect capability, authority and availability, and handle gaps by upskilling or moving responsibilities.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.2; PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3.2

test.q: Saltmarsh's service design lead already prioritizes the team's work with tenants and facilitates its iterations. The project manager has no budget for another person. Which approach fits PRINCE2 Agile guidance on roles?
options: Combine roles where capability and time allow
Hire a new person for each role that is open
Pause the iteration until each role is staffed
Ask the board to perform the open team roles
test.why: Roles can be combined or shared when one person per role is impractical (4.3.2), matched to capability, authority and availability.

whyNot.1: Hiring for every role is not required by the method and the budget is fixed.
whyNot.2: Pausing delivery is unnecessary when roles can be combined.
whyNot.3: Board members direct the project; they do not take delivery team roles.

explain.body: Plan how people work together, virtual, in person or hybrid. Sync co-location days for key people and teams; allow less structured time online. Mandating co-location or adding formal agendas is unlikely to build it.

test.q: Draycott's software team works at Factory A, while maintenance engineers at Factory B join trials online and feel like outsiders. Which action is MOST LIKELY to build social cohesion?
options: Move all Factory B engineers to Factory A
Run trials with a strict, timed agenda online
Send Factory B a weekly written trial summary
Sync on-site days for key people at both sites
test.why: Syncing co-location days for key people and teams, focused on key relationships, helps cohesion in teams at a distance (4.3.3).

whyNot.0: Mandating co-location is unlikely to build cohesion and disrupts maintenance cover.
whyNot.1: A strict agenda makes sessions efficient, not cohesive.
whyNot.2: A written summary shares information but builds no relationships.

explain.body: Co-location and remote arrangements with tools: project management team structure. Specific responsibilities: role descriptions. Decision rights per area: delegation matrix. Skills and gaps: team skill matrix.

test.q: At Pinewick, the project manager wants a single view of which store team members can run training, which can set up collection points, and where nobody yet has the skill. What should be created?
options: A delegation matrix
A team skill matrix
The role descriptions
A delegation poker set
test.why: A team skill matrix gives an overview of capabilities, strengths, gaps and development areas (7.4.1).

whyNot.0: A delegation matrix shows decision authority, not skills.
whyNot.2: Role descriptions set out responsibilities, not who has which skills.
whyNot.3: Delegation poker is a technique for agreeing decision-making levels.
